newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Full text of ACPC coffee statement in Costa Rica.
newsitem.headline: Full text of ACPC coffee statement in Costa Rica.

text.p: Below follows the full text of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries' (ACPC) technical group meeting in Costa Rica. The one-day meeting ended late Saturday.
The meeting was attended by Brazil, Colombia, Ivory Coast, El Salvador, Indonesia and Uganda and also by Costa Rica, Honduras and IACO as observers.
After an extensive analysis of the market situation, on the basis of a document prepared by the secretariat, the group noted with satisfaction:
1) World consumption is increasing and is now just over 75 million green coffee equivalent (60-kg) bags in consuming countries and 25 million bags in producing countries.
2) ACPC forecasts green coffee production for 1996/1997 at 99 million (60-kg) bags.
3) Visible stocks in consuming countries are believed to be currently around 8.5 million bags, in with expectations of the export programme.
The group also noted the development of the ACPC export programme for the semester July/December 1996 and following consultations with delegates, concluded that the original target will be achieved.
The group also recalled the decision taken by the (full ACPC) council on May 17, 1996 that stated:

"The technical group will meet regularly at the end of the quarter to assess the implementation of the programme. If the situation so merits, the chairman of the ACPC shall convene a council meeting which will decide on the measures to be applied."

In light of this decision by the council, it was agreed that prior to the next meeting of the technical group, to be held up to mid-February, the chairman will consult with members and will decide if the council should have an extraordinary meeting to consider the recommendations on the export programme to be made by the technical group.

The group instructed the secretariat to extend its work to further analysis of consumption patterns and also to verify both consumer and producer stocks. The secretariat will present a proposal to the next meeting of the technical group for funding of this latter project.
